titleEn: Getting a SIM card in a new country
titleTh: ซื้อซิมการ์ดในต่างประเทศ
scenarioSentences: You arrived in a new country yesterday.
You need a local SIM card.
You use your phone for maps.
You go to a phone shop.
Ms. Kato works there.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, I'd like a SIM card. I've just arrived here.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kato
dialogue.text: Welcome! How long are you staying?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: About three weeks. I need lots of data for maps.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kato
dialogue.text: We have a one-week plan and a one-month plan.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: What's the difference in price?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kato
dialogue.text: One week is fifteen dollars. One month is thirty, with twice the data.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The monthly plan is better value, then. I'll take that one.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kato
dialogue.text: Great. I'll need to see your passport, please.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Here you are. Can you put the card in for me?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Kato
dialogue.text: Of course. It'll be ready in five minutes.

titleTh: ตั้งชมรมอ่านหนังสือ
scenarioSentences: You and Elif both love reading.
You want to start a book club.
Some classmates are also interested.
You need to make a few decisions.
You meet Elif after class.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Elif, five people want to join our book club. When should we meet?

dialogue.speaker: Elif
dialogue.text: Once a week might be too much. People are busy.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: You're right. How about every two weeks?

dialogue.speaker: Elif
dialogue.text: That's better. It gives everyone enough time to finish the book.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Which book should we start with?

dialogue.speaker: Elif
dialogue.text: Something short and fun. Maybe a mystery novel?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. I'll suggest three and everyone can vote.

dialogue.speaker: Elif
dialogue.text: Where should we meet? My apartment is quite small.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The library has a free room. Let's book it for next Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Elif
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll send a message to the group tonight.

titleEn: Renting a room in a shared house
titleTh: ขอเช่าห้องในบ้านที่อยู่ร่วมกัน
scenarioSentences: You need a cheaper place to live.
A room in a shared house is available.
Mr. Hardy owns the house.
You visit the room today.
You have some questions for him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks for showing me the room, Mr. Hardy. How much is the rent?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hardy
dialogue.text: It's four hundred dollars a month, including electricity and internet.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fine. Are there any house rules?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hardy
dialogue.text: No parties, and keep the kitchen clean.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No problem. I'm a quiet person. Do you need a deposit?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hardy
dialogue.text: Yes, one month's rent. You'll get it back when you leave.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay. When could I move in?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hardy
dialogue.text: The room is free from the end of this month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So I could move in on the first of next month?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Hardy
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'll send you the agreement tomorrow.

titleTh: รักษาอาการบาดเจ็บจากการเล่นกีฬา
scenarioSentences: You hurt your knee playing soccer.
It has been sore for a week.
You have a big game next month.
Dr. Kumar treats sports injuries.
You see her at the clinic.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Dr. Kumar, my knee still hurts a week after I fell.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Kumar
dialogue.text: Let me check. Does it hurt when you bend it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, especially when I go down the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Kumar
dialogue.text: It's not broken, but the muscles around it are weak.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Can I still play in next month's game?

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Kumar
dialogue.text: Maybe, if you're careful. No soccer for three weeks.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Three weeks? What should I do instead?

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Kumar
dialogue.text: Do these exercises twice a day. Swimming is fine too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay. Should I come back for another check?

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Kumar
dialogue.text: Yes, in two weeks. We'll see how it's healing.

titleTh: ยกเลิกบริการดูหนังรายเดือน
scenarioSentences: You pay for a movie service every month.
You have not watched anything for weeks.
You want to save some money.
You call customer service.
Ms. Jensen answers the phone.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Jensen. I'd like to cancel my movie plan, please.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Jensen
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. May I ask why?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I haven't used it for two months.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Jensen
dialogue.text: I understand. Would you like our cheaper five-dollar plan instead?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No, thanks. I really don't need it at the moment.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Jensen
dialogue.text: All right. Your plan will end on the thirtieth of this month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Will I get a refund for this month?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Jensen
dialogue.text: No, but you can keep watching until the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fine. Can you send me an email to confirm?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Jensen
dialogue.text: Of course. You'll get it in a few minutes.

titleEn: Planning a vegetarian menu for guests
titleTh: วางเมนูมังสวิรัติให้แขก
scenarioSentences: You and Rafael are having a dinner party.
Eight friends are coming.
Two of them do not eat meat.
You want to cook one main dish.
You plan the menu together.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Rafael, two of our guests don't eat meat. What should we cook?

dialogue.speaker: Rafael
dialogue.text: We could make chicken for most people and something else for them.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's two main dishes, though. It's too much work.

dialogue.speaker: Rafael
dialogue.text: True. What about one vegetarian dish for everyone?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. How about a vegetable curry with rice?

dialogue.speaker: Rafael
dialogue.text: I love that. Is it too spicy for some people?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We can make it mild and put chili sauce on the table.

dialogue.speaker: Rafael
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll make a salad and bread too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Let's go shopping on Friday after work.

dialogue.speaker: Rafael
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll write the shopping list tonight.

titleEn: Moving a job interview to another day
titleTh: ขอเลื่อนวันสัมภาษณ์งาน
scenarioSentences: You applied for a part-time job.
Ms. Monroe invited you to an interview.
It is on Tuesday at ten.
You have a final exam then.
You call her to explain.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Ms. Monroe. Thank you for inviting me to the interview.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Monroe
dialogue.text: You're welcome. We're looking forward to meeting you on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, but I have a final exam at that time.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Monroe
dialogue.text: I see. Could you come in the afternoon instead?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The exam goes until four, so that's too late.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Monroe
dialogue.text: Then how about Thursday? I'm free at ten or at three.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thursday at ten would be perfect.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Monroe
dialogue.text: Great. I'll change the time and send you an email.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you very much for your help.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Monroe
dialogue.text: No problem. Good luck with your exam!

titleTh: หัดนั่งรถไฟใต้ดินในเมืองใหม่
scenarioSentences: You moved to a new city.
You need the metro for work.
The map looks very confusing.
Your friend Tariq has lived here for years.
You ask him for help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Tariq, I need to take the metro to work. How do tickets work?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.text: You can buy single tickets, but a travel card is cheaper.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Where can I get a travel card?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.text: At any station. You can add money to it later.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. My office is near the central market. Which line is best?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.text: Take line two. It's the green one on the map.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Do I need to change lines?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.text: No, it goes straight there. It takes about twenty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll buy a card at the station tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.text: Good. Avoid eight o'clock if you can. It's really crowded.

titleTh: เปิดร้านค้าออนไลน์เล็ก ๆ
scenarioSentences: Your friend Amara makes bags by hand.
People often ask to buy them.
She wants to sell them online.
She asks you for advice.
You are good at taking photos.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Amara, your bags are amazing. Have you thought about selling them online?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Yes, but I don't know where to start.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: First, you need good photos. I can take them for you.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: That would be great. What price should I ask?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Compare prices on other websites. Similar bags sell for about thirty dollars.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Each bag takes me four hours, so thirty seems low.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then try forty and see if people buy them.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Okay. How many bags should I make first?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Start with ten. If they sell quickly, you can make more.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Good plan. Let's take the photos this Saturday.

titleEn: Getting help with a computer virus
titleTh: ขอให้ช่างช่วยกำจัดไวรัสคอมพิวเตอร์
scenarioSentences: Your laptop has become very slow.
Strange windows keep opening on the screen.
You think it has a virus.
Mr. Fraser is the IT technician.
You take it to him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Fraser, my laptop is slow, and strange ads keep popping up.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fraser
dialogue.text: That sounds like a virus. Have you downloaded anything recently?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I downloaded a free game last week. Was that it?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fraser
dialogue.text: Probably. I'll remove it and clean the whole laptop.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Will I lose my files? My project is on there.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fraser
dialogue.text: I'll back up your files first, so they'll be safe.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. How long will it take?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fraser
dialogue.text: About two hours. You can pick it up after lunch.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. How can I stop this from happening again?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Fraser
dialogue.text: Only download from websites you trust, and back up every week.
